x: Under Article 155, the President appoints the Governor by warrant under hand and seal. Article 153 provides a Governor for each State, 156 the term, and 159 the oath.
t: Recall Articles 153 to 159 in order.

x: Option D is incorrect: a Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature, and must give up any such seat on appointment. They must be a citizen, at least 35, and hold no office of profit.
t: Recall the Governor's qualifications under Articles 157 and 158.

x: Both are true: the Governor's term is five years, but they hold office during the President's pleasure (Article 156), so they can be removed earlier or stay on until a successor takes over. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the President's pleasure explains the flexible term.

x: All three are correct: the Governor's emoluments are charged on the State's fund, a Governor of two States is paid in shares the President fixes, and the High Court's Chief Justice administers the oath (Article 159).
t: Recall who swears in the Governor and how pay is shared.

x: Article 153 provides a Governor for each State, 154 vests executive power in them, 159 covers the oath, and 213 ordinances. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall Articles 153, 154, 159 and 213.

x: Both are true: under Article 161, the Governor grants pardons only for offences against State laws, and R lists the kinds of relief available. The list does not explain the limit to State laws, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a list of reliefs explains a limit of scope.

x: Option C is incorrect: Sarojini Naidu, India's first woman Governor, governed Uttar Pradesh. Her daughter Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
t: Discriminate the two Naidus' States.
o: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Padmaja Naidu was the daughter of Sarojini Naidu.

x: All four are discretionary: choosing a Chief Minister in a hung Assembly, dismissing a ministry that has lost its majority, reserving a bill for the President, and recommending President's Rule.
t: Recall the Governor's discretionary powers.

x: The President appoints the Governor by warrant under hand and seal (Article 155), the Governor holds office during the President's pleasure, makes ordinances under Article 213 and pardons under Article 161. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall Articles 156, 161 and 213.
s:
Match the features in List-I with the corresponding provisions or descriptions in List-II:
List-I
(a) Appointment of the Governor
(b) Removal of the Governor
(c) Ordinance-making power of the Governor
(d) Pardoning power of the Governor

List-II
(i) Pleasure of the President
(ii) Article 213
(iii) Warrant under the President's hand and seal (Article 155)
(iv) Article 161

x: Other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the Chief Minister's advice. The Governor appoints the Advocate-General under Article 165, the State Election Commissioner under Article 243K, and State PSC members under Article 316. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the Article under which the Governor makes each appointment.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Other Ministers
(b) Advocate-General
(c) State Election Commissioner
(d) Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission

List-II
(i) Article 165
(ii) Appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister
(iii) Article 243K
(iv) Article 316

x: All five are correct: the Governor can seek information (Article 167), is part of the State Legislature (Article 168), and summons, prorogues and dissolves it.
t: Recall the Governor's legislative powers.

x: Both are true: under Article 176, the Governor addresses the State Legislature, and under Article 200, assents to bills, withholds assent or reserves them for the President.
t: Recall Articles 176 and 200.

x: Both are true: in States with a Legislative Council, the Governor nominates one-sixth of its members from literature, science, art, co-operation and social service.
t: Recall the Governor's one-sixth share.

x: Under Article 233, the Governor appoints district judges in consultation with the High Court.
t: Recall Article 233.

x: All five are correct: Article 361 gives the Governor immunity, no criminal case can be started during the term, and civil suits need two months' notice. The President serves five years and is removed by impeachment.
t: Check each statement on its own facts.

x: The President's ordinances are under Article 123 and pardons under 72 (all cases). The Governor's ordinances are under 213 and pardons under 161 (State laws only). The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
t: Pair the President's Articles (123, 72) with the Governor's (213, 161).

x: Both are true: the President has very little discretion, and the Governor, by comparison, has more. The Governor's wider discretion does not explain why the President's is limited, so R does not explain A.
t: Contrast the President's discretion with the Governor's.

x: Both are true: Jammu and Kashmir's head of State was called Sadr-e-Riyasat until 1965, when the title became Governor.
t: Recall the 1965 change of title.

x: Two are correct: the Governor runs the State Contingency Fund and is appointed, not elected. Statement 2 is false because anti-defection cases go to the Speaker; the Governor decides only Article 191 disqualifications, on the Election Commission's advice.
t: Discriminate Article 191 disqualification (Governor) from Tenth Schedule defection (Speaker).

x: Both are true: the Governor can reserve a bill for the President against ministerial advice because the Governor is not bound by that advice in every matter. R explains A.
t: Ask whether limited discretion explains acting against advice.

x: Reserving a Bill for the President under Article 200 is a constitutional discretionary power of the Governor. Summoning and addressing the legislature and issuing ordinances are done on ministerial advice.
t: Discriminate discretionary powers from powers used on advice.
o: Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
Promulgating an Ordinance when the Legislature is not in session

x: Article 371(2) gives the Maharashtra Governor special responsibility for regional development boards, the Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas with a report to the President, Article 167 entitles the Governor to information from the Chief Minister, and the Sixth Schedule creates Autonomous District Councils. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Link each provision to the specific power or duty of the Governor it creates.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 371(2)
(b) Fifth Schedule
(c) Article 167
(d) Sixth Schedule

List-II
(i) Special responsibility for development boards in Vidarbha, Marathwada and the rest of Maharashtra
(ii) Administration of Scheduled Areas, with a report to the President
(iii) Right to be informed by the Chief Minister of the Council's decisions
(iv) Autonomous District Councils in tribal areas of the North-East

x: The Chief Minister is the real executive head of the State and heads the Council of Ministers. The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head, like the President at the Centre.
t: Discriminate the nominal head from the real executive.

x: Both are true: under Article 167, the Chief Minister must tell the Governor the Council's decisions and legislative plans, which is why the Chief Minister is the link between them. R explains A.
t: Recall the Chief Minister's duties under Article 167.

x: Option D is incorrect: the Chief Minister answers to the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council. The Governor heads the State and the Chief Minister the government.
t: Recall which House the ministry answers to.

x: Both are true: the Governor appoints the leader of the Assembly majority as Chief Minister, and a non-member can be appointed but must enter the legislature within six months.
t: Recall the six-month rule for non-members.

x: I and II are correct: under the 91st Amendment (2003), the ministry, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the Assembly, with a minimum of 12. III is false because the base is the Assembly, not the Council.
t: Recall the base for the 15% limit.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of the State Council of Ministers:
I. The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
II. The minimum strength in smaller States is 12, including the Chief Minister.
III. The 15% limit is calculated on the total strength of the Legislative Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister and E.M.S. Namboodiripad the first non-Congress one. The President appoints the Chief Ministers of Delhi and Puducherry, and the Governor swears in a Chief Minister. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each first and each appointing authority.

x: Three involve the Governor: appointing the Chief Minister, administering the oath and receiving the resignation. The President appoints the Chief Ministers of Delhi and Puducherry under Article 239AA.
t: Find the Union Territory exception.

x: Both are true: under Article 164(2), the ministry is collectively answerable to the Assembly, which is why a passed no-confidence motion forces the whole ministry, Chief Minister included, to resign. R explains A.
t: Ask whether resigning together explains collective responsibility.

x: Both are true: Article 163 provides a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor. Both statements say the same thing.
t: Recall Article 163.

x: The Chief Minister chooses Ministers, allocates portfolios, can recommend a Minister's removal, and must give the Governor information. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each power to its description.

x: A Chief Minister can belong to either House: the Assembly, or the Legislative Council where one exists.
t: Recall that the Chief Minister can come from either House.

x: Both are true duties under Article 167: putting a Minister's decision before the Council, and giving the Governor information. Two separate duties do not explain each other, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether one duty explains a different duty.

x: The Chief Minister leads the Assembly and speaks for the government, and advises the Governor on summoning and proroguing the legislature and on dissolving the Assembly. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each role to its description.
